nodes.name: Electrochemical Exfoliation
nodes.procedure: The fabrication of NiPS3 crystals was achieved through the conventional chemical vapor transport method. Subsequently, an electrochemical workstation (Autolab PGSTAT204) was used to perform electrochemical exfoliation in a two-electrode configuration (Pt wire as the counter electrode and bulk NiPS3 as the working electrode). The electrolytic solution was produced by dissolving 0.05M tetrabutylammonium tetrafluoroborate (98%) in 30 ml of N,N'-dimethylformamide (99.5%). Throughout the exfoliation procedure, a constant bias voltage of -5V was applied to the working electrode, resulting in a brown suspension.

nodes.name: Ultrasonic Dispersion and Drying
nodes.procedure: This suspension was subsequently exposed to an ice bath ultrasonic process at 300W for 90 min to further disperse the NiPS3 nanosheets. The resulting material was washed with ethanol five times to eliminate the residual exfoliation electrolyte on the surface of nanosheets and then dried under vacuum at 60°C overnight to yield EE-NiPS3 powder.

nodes.name: Fe/NiPS3 Surface Modification
nodes.procedure: First, 20 mg of EE-NiPS3 powder was ultrasonically dispersed in 5 ml of deionized water to obtain suspension A. Second, a preheated aqueous solution containing Fe3+ ions was prepared: Iron(III) chloride hexahydrate (0.101g, 0.37 mmol) and sodium nitrate (0.212g, 2.49 mmol) were dissolved in 45 ml of deionized water and kept at 100°C under the protection of argon for at least 5 min to obtain a deep orange solution B. Then, the preheated suspension A was quickly injected into solution B and kept for 10s at 100°C. Last, Fe/NiPS3 powder was obtained by washing the product with deionized water/ethanol several times and drying overnight under vacuum at 60°C.

nodes.description: OER performance in 1 M KOH on glassy carbon electrode without iR compensation
nodes.source_text: After loading on planar glassy carbon electrodes, the OER catalytic properties of different samples were evaluated in a 1 M KOH electrolyte (Fig. 4, A and B). The Fe/NiPS₃-4 catalyst can deliver the OER with low overpotential (η₁₀, at 10mAcm⁻²) of 242mV and a small Tafel slope of 78.1mVdec⁻¹ without Ohmic drop (iR) compensation.

nodes.description: SOER performance in natural seawater (1 M KOH + Bohai seawater) on glassy carbon
nodes.source_text: Furthermore, the SOER catalysis was assessed in an electrolyte prepared by seawater (from Bohai Sea) mixed with 1M KOH, as shown in Fig. 4E. The Fe/NiPS₃ electrocatalyst presents the low η₁₀ of 264mV and a small Tafel slope of 59.9mVdec⁻¹, which is superior to EE-NiPS (370mV 120.6mVdec⁻¹) and commercial RuO₂ (384mV,132.8mVdec⁻¹).

nodes.characterization_summary: Thickness of EE-NiPS₃ nanosheets is approximately 2.70 nm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The atomic force microscope test results indicate that the thickness of EE-NiPS₃ is approximately 2.70 nm (fig. S14).

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM shows Fe/NiPS₃ exhibits notably granular rough surface morphology compared to EE-NiPS₃ nanosheets.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Compared with EE-NiPS₃ nanosheets, the Fe/NiPS₃ sample exhibits a notably granular rough surface morphology (Fig. 2D and fig. S15D).

nodes.characterization_summary: Aberration-corrected BF-STEM confirms nanosheet morphology well maintained after Fe³⁺-NiPS₃ reaction.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The aberration-corrected bright-field scanning transmission electron microscopy (BF-STEM) image (Fig. 2E) ... illustrate that the nanosheet morphology is well maintained.

nodes.characterization_summary: HR-TEM shows surface reconstruction after Fe introduction with d-spacing of 0.247 nm for NiPS₃ (131) plane.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The high-resolution TEM (HR-TEM) images of Fe/NiPS₃ indicate the surface reconstruction after Fe introduction, and the d-spacing of 0.247 nm is recognized for the NiPS₃ (131) plane (Fig. 2F).

nodes.characterization_summary: SAED identifies (131)/(201)/(132)/(331) crystal planes of NiPS₃ in Fe/NiPS₃.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The selected area electron diffraction pattern (SAED; Fig. 2G) of Fe/NiPS₃ identifies the (131)/(201)/(132)/(331) crystal planes of NiPS₃.

nodes.characterization_summary: EDX mapping confirms homogeneous Fe/Ni/P/S elemental distribution in Fe/NiPS₃ nanosheets.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The element mappings in Fig. 2H and fig. S21 confirm the homogeneous Fe/Ni/P/S elemental distribution in the Fe/NiPS₃ nanosheets.

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD shows peaks at 13.9°/28.1°/31.0°/36.1°/58.2° corresponding to (001)/(002)/(130)/(131)/(004) planes of NiPS₃ for Fe/NiPS with no Fe-related peaks.
nodes.evidence_snippet: For Fe/NiPS, the XRD peaks at 13.9°/28.1°/31.0°/36.1°/58.2° correspond to the (001)/(002)/(130)/(131)/(004) planes of NiPS₃ (29), and no Fe-related peaks can be observed.

nodes.characterization_summary: Raman shows typical E_g/A_{1g} phonon modes with slight redshifts over EE-NiPS due to hindered vibration from Fe introduction.
nodes.evidence_snippet: It shows the typical E_g/A_{1g} phonon modes with slight redshifts over EE-NiPS, which may be related to the hindered vibration of the NiPS₃ substrate atoms due to Fe introduction (30).

nodes.characterization_summary: FTIR shows Fe/NiPS exhibits higher surface O-H vibration intensity and stronger water affinity than EE-NiPS.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 3C displays the Fourier transform infrared (FTIR) spectra of these samples, in which Fe/NiPS exhibits a higher surface O-H vibration intensity and stronger water affinity than EE-NiPS.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni 2p peak shifts -0.23 eV indicating reduction in Ni valence state; Fe 2p spectrum shows two kinds of Fe{III} coordination sites successfully introduced.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Compared to EE-NiPS, the Ni 2p peak of Fe/NiPS exhibits a shift of approximately -0.23 eV ... The Fe 2p spectrum in Fig. 3E also suggests that two kinds of Fe{III} coordination sites were successfully introduced into the Fe/NiPS₃ sample.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni K-edge XANES shows slight downshift indicating reduced Ni valence; Fe K-edge XANES edge upshift reveals Fe valence +3.37 in Fe/NiPS₃.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Compared to EE-NiPS, the slight downshift of the XANES edge indicates the reduced Ni valence in Fe/NiPS₃ (Fig. 3F, inset) ... The Fe valence is calculated as high as +3.37 in the Fe/NiPS₃ material from the linear fit of XANES data (fig. S26).

nodes.characterization_summary: ESR shows much higher peak intensity for Fe/NiPS₃ than EE-NiPS₃ ascertaining active role of Fe doping in increasing unpaired electrons.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Fe/NiPS₃ is observed with much higher peak intensity than that of EE-NiPS₃, ascertaining the active role of Fe doping in the increase of unpaired electrons (43).

nodes.characterization_summary: SQUID magnetic hysteresis loops show larger slopes for Fe/NiPS₃ indicating enhanced magnetism; μ_eff = 4.29 μ_B at RT with ~3.4 unpaired electrons.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As displayed with magnetic hysteresis loops (Fig. 5B), the slopes of Fe/NiPS₃ ... are larger than that of EE-NiPS₃ ... The μ_eff of Fe/NiPS₃ at RT (4.29 μ_B) is higher than ... EE-NiPS₃ (1.76 μ_B).

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni K-edge FT-EXAFS shows Ni-S peak shift from 2.28 to 2.31 Å and Ni-Ni peak shift from 3.40 to 3.37 Å reflecting asymmetric structure distortion after Fe doping.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Fourier transform extended Xray absorption fine structure (FT-EXAFS) spectra were further analyzed ... Compared to EE-NiPS, the Ni-S characteristic peak shifts toward a higher R value (2.28 to 2.31 Å) in Fe/NiPS₃, while a lower R value shift (3.40 to 3.37 Å) is observed in the Ni-Ni characteristic peak.
